Order 
This is second application filed by the applicants under Section 482 of BNSS (Section 438 of the Cr.P.C.) seeking anticipatory bail in connection with FIR/Crime No.672/2023 dated 16.10.2023 registered at Police Station Rahatgarh District Sagar for the offences punishable under Sections 409,
420, 417, 418, 120B, 201, 467 of IPC and Sections 13(1)(a) and 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

Earlier application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn by this Court vide order dated 13.03.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No.8020/2025 with liberty of surrender before the trial Court and apply for regular bail as expeditiously as possible preferably on the same day.
2. Learned counsel for the applicants contends that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
It is contended by the counsel that the present applicant was not initially implicated.
The charge- sheet in the matter was filed.

As many as 6 prosecution witnesses were NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21756 2 MCRC-20041-2025 examined and at that stage, the prosecution came up with the supplementary charge-sheet which was to be filed in respect of co-accused who was absconding but after filing of the charge-sheet, the prosecution has ventured upon to implicate the present applicant also and such a course is impermissible in view of the Section 193(9) of BNSS.

It is contended by the counsel that without prior concurrence of the Court,
further investigation in the matter where the trial is pending, is not permitted hence, the applicant deserves to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: 3. Per contra, counsel for the State has opposed the application and submitted that the present applicant is guilty of commission of offence and he is the beneficiaries to whom there are illegal allotments of plots, hence no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.

4. Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.
5.
A perusal of the record prima facie reflects that the charge-sheet in the matter initially was not filed against the applicant.
Out of 3 co-accused persons, one of the co-accused was absconding, and therefore, the supplementary charge-sheet was filed later on.
However, at this stage, the present applicant has also been implicated.
Thus in the present case the debatable issue is as regards applicability of the proviso of Section 193(9) of BNSS.
Co-accused persons have already been released on anticipatory bail by this Court on the same ground.
5. Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court deems it to be a fit case to release the applicant on anticipatory bail.
Therefore, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21756 3 MCRC-20041-2025 application is allowed.

6. It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicants shall be enlarged on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer for his appearance before him during the course of investigation or before the trial Court concerned during trial, as the case may be.
7. It is further directed that the applicant shall abide by all the conditions as enumerated under Section 482(2) of the BNSS.
8. Accordingly, M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
